chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Malik ibn 'Atiyyah from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who had a slave father, and the father's wife was a mukatabah (slave woman contracted for manumission) who had paid part of what was due to her. The son of the slave said to her, 'Would you like me to assist you in your manumission contract until you pay what is due to you, on the condition that you do not have the option to choose to stay with your master if you acquire your own freedom?' She said, 'Yes.' So he gave her the manumission contract on the condition that she would not have the option afterwards.
He (the Imam) said, 'She does not have the option; Muslims are bound by their conditions.'

key_terms.اَلْخِيَارُ: The option or right to choose (specifically between staying with or leaving the master)
key_terms.اَلْمُسْلِمُونَ عِنْدَ شُرُوطِهِمْ: Muslims are bound by their conditions (a key legal maxim)
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَةٌ: Manumission contract where a slave pays a fixed sum for freedom

ai.seo_question: What is the legal validity of attaching conditions to a slave's manumission contract regarding the right to choose?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the specific contractual condition waiving the mukatabah's right of choice (khiyar), illustrating the flexibility of fiqh in personal status agreements. This ruling is grounded in the Quranic principle that Muslims are bound by their stipulations, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the validity of non-contradictory conditions in contracts. The narration highlights the practical application of 'al-muslimun 'ala shurutihim' in ensuring contractual certainty between masters and slaves.
